I.A. No. 03 of 2021
In
CRLA No. 314 of 2021
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. S.C. Bhatt, Advocate for the 
appellant/applicant.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder 
for the State.
The appellant/applicant is in judicial 
custody, post conviction under Sections 376 
(2), 363 and 366 IPC. He has sought short 
term bail on the grounds that his cousin is 
to marry on 26.11.2021; the family is a 
joint family and his wife is also to deliver a 
child in the third week of November, 2021. 
There are emotional moments for the 
appellant.
Heard learned counsel for the 
applicant as well as learned State Counsel 
and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the applicant 
would submit that the applicant is the eldest 
son in the joint family; his cousin is to 
marry on 26.11.2021; his wife is also to 
deliver a child in the third week of 
November, 2021. These are emotional 
moments for him, therefore, he may be 
granted short term bail.
Learned counsel for the applicant has 
also submitted that the factum has been 
verified by Sub Inspector Babita Tamta of 
the concerned police station. 
On 18.11.2021, the State was given 
time to verify the contents of the short term 
bail application. 
Today, the learned State Counsel 
states that he has not received any 
instructions as yet. 
This is very very sorry state of 
affairs.  Having considered, this Court is of 
the view that purely on humanitarian 
ground, the applicant may be granted short 
term bail for a period of one week, from the 
date of his release.
Short term bail application (I.A. No. 
03 of 2021) is allowed.
The applicant shall be enlarged on 
short term bail only for a period of one 
week from the date of his release, on his 
executing a personal bond and furnishing 
two reliable sureties, each of the like 
amount to the satisfaction of the court 
concerned. It is further directed that, on 
expiry of the period of short term bail, the 
applicant shall surrender before the court 
concerned and intimation to this effect shall 
also be given to this Court. 
List on 01.12.2021.
Let a certified copy of this order be 
issued today itself on payment of usual 
charges.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 22.11.2021

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Bail Application No. 1 of 2021
In
Criminal Appeal No. 314 of 2021
Sandeep Singh ......Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ….Respondent
Present:
Mr. S.C. Bhatt, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, D.A.G. for the State.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)
Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment 
and order dated 04.09.2021/ 06.09.2021, passed in Special 
Sessions Trial No.114 of 2017, by the court of 
FTC/Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, POCSO, 
Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar. By the impugned 
judgment and order, the appellant has been convicted 
under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2) IPC and Section 6 of the 
Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for 
short, “the Act”) and sentenced under Sections 363, 366, 
376 (2) IPC. In this appeal, the appellant has filed a bail 
application.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and 
perused the record. 2
3. According to the prosecution case, the appellant 
on 26.12.2016, at about 4:00-5:00 PM took away the victim 
girl, who was 17 years of age then on his motorcycle. The 
mother of the victim tried to stop her, she raised alarm, but 
she was not successful in her attempt. Subsequently, the 
victim was recovered. Her statement was recorded. She 
revealed that the appellant raped her in the Bank where he 
was working and under the threat of making the intimate 
photos viral raped her on multiple times. This is what the 
victim stated in the court. There have been other witnesses 
also, who supported the prosecution case. The court below 
based on the school record and other material recorded the 
finding that the date of birth of the victim is 17.09.1999, 
which means that she was 17 years of age on the date of 
occurrence. It was also established that the appellant was 
married having two children when the judgment was 
recorded. Although, today a statement is given that now the 
appellant has three children including a four month’s baby 
girl.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit 
that the appellant was on bail during trial. He has three 
children. One of them is four months old, who is to be 
vaccinated. The father of the appellant is 70 years old. He is  3
suffering from spondylitis. In her statement, in para 41, the 
victim has admitted that during investigation or at the stage 
of recording statement under Section 164 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, “the Code”). she did 
not reveal the specific date when the incident took place. 
Therefore, it is argued that it is a case fit for bail.
5. On the other hand, learned State counsel would 
submit that the victim was minor. She was just 17 years of 
age when she was taken away from the custody of her 
father. The accused was 28 years old at the time of incident 
He was married having three children. The victim and the 
witnesses, her mother, father and brother have supported 
the prosecution case. Hence, it is not a fit case for bail.
6. The grounds for bail which are available to an
accused during trial are quite distinct and slightly different 
than the grounds that may be available to a convict in 
appeal. The presumption of innocence which an accused 
carries with him during trial is not available to him at the 
stage of appeal because today he is not an accused but a 
convict.
7. The victim in her statement given in the court 
has supported the prosecution case and has narrated as to  4
how the offence has been committed and she was taken 
away by the appellant. Her mother and father have also 
supported the prosecution case. The date of birth of the 
victim is conclusively recorded by the court as 17.09.1999. 
It means she was 17 years of age on the date of incident. 
The appellant was 33 years of age when he was examined 
under Section 313 of the Code on 18.10.2019, it means he 
was 30 years of age on the date of incident.
8. Having considered the gravity of offence, this 
Court is of the view that it is not a case fit for bail.
Accordingly, the bail application deserves to be rejected.
9. The bail application is rejected.
10. List this matter for final hearing.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 05.05.2022 
Jitendra

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 314 of 2021
Sandeep Singh ….....Appellant
 
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ….….Respondent
Present:-
Mr. M.S. Pal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Sachin, 
Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Deputy Advocate General along with Mr. 
Balvinder Singh, Brief Holder for the State.
 
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment 
and order dated 04.09.2021/06.09.2021, passed in Special 
Sessions Trial No. 114 of 2017, by the court of FTC/Additional 
Sessions Judge/Special Judge, POCSO, Rudrapur, District 
Udham Singh Nagar. By the impugned judgment and order, 
the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363, 366, 
376 (2) IPC and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from 
Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, “the Act”) and sentenced 
under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2) IPC. 
2. In this appeal, the appellant has filed a short term 
bail application, on the ground that his father is unwell, who 
has an appointment at AIIMS, Rishikesh on 05.09.2022. There 
is no other person in the family, who could take his father to 
the hospital, therefore, short term bail for a short period may 
be granted. 2
3. Learned Senior Advocate appearing for the 
appellant would submit that appellant is the only son of his 
father; his father is unwell and the appellant has to take his
father for medical examination at AIIMS, Rishikesh. 
4. Along with the short term bail application, a
discharge slip of Civil Hospital, Khatima, which records the 
Diagnosis Gastritis (Pain Abdomen) referred to a higher centre. 
It does not reveal the investigations. An affidavit in support of 
the short term bail application, has been filed by a person, 
namely, Jaswant Singh, who is alleged to be the relative of the 
appellant and doing pairvi. The father of the appellant is 
stated to be 65 years of age.
5. Having considered all the attending factors, this 
Court is of the view that there is no sufficient ground to grant 
short term bail. Accordingly, the short term bail application 
deserves to be rejected.
6. Accordingly, the short term bail application (IA No. 
5 of 2022) is rejected. 
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 02.09.2022

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Short Term Bail Application (IA) No. 6 of 2023
In
Criminal Appeal No. 314 of 2021
Sandeep Singh ....Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ….Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Nandan Arya, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Amit Bhatt, D.A.G. for the State.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Instant appeal has been preferred against the 
judgment and orders dated 04.09.2021/06.09.2021 
passed in Special Sessions Trial No. 114 of 2017, by the 
Court of FTC/Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, 
POCSO, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar.By the 
impugned judgment and order, the appellants has been 
convicted under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2) IPC and 
Section 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual 
Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced thereunder. 
2. Heard on short term bail application.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant would 
submit that the appellant has one year six months old
daughter, who is with his wife. His parents are aged. His  2
daughter has got a fracture on her leg and the Doctor has 
referred her to a higher centre.
4. Learned State counsel, under instructions 
would submit that the factual aspects, as narrated by the 
learned counsel for the appellant are corrected.
5. Without adverting to the merits, purely on 
humanitarian ground, this Court is of the view that the 
appellant may be enlarged on short term bail for a 
period of two weeks.
6. Let the appellant be released on short term 
bail during the pendency of this appeal for a period of 
two weeks from the date of his release, subject to his 
furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of 
the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court 
concerned.
7. After expiry of the period of short term bail, 
the appellant shall surrender before the court 
concerned and an information shall be forwarded to this 
Court. 3
8. The short term bail application is allowed 
accordingly.
9. List this matter on 05.12.2023.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 15.09.2023
Jitendra

Present Mr. Pramod Kumar, counsel 
holding brief of Mr. Nandan Arya, counsel for 
the appellant.
2. Present Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, AGA 
along with Mr. Pramod Tiwari, Brief Holder 
for the State. 
3. Heard on the time extension application 
(IA No.9 of 2023). 
4. Counsel for the appellant would submit 
that the applicant/accused was granted short 
term bail application as his daughter was to 
undergo surgery for fracture in her right leg; 
that, the period of short term bail has expired 
on 07.12.2023 and he has to surrender today, 
however, the medical necessity is still there. 
5. Per contra, counsel for the State would 
submit that by order dated 15.09.2023 short 
term bail was granted to the applicant/accused 
for a period of two weeks; that, on 06.10.2023 
it was extended for a further period of six 
weeks; that, on 10.11.2023 it was again 
extended for three weeks. She would further 
submit that Annexure No.1 is the discharge 
summary obtained from the Swastik Hospital, 
according to which, daughter of the 
applicant/accused was discharged on 
03.12.2023 itself. 
6. Counsel for the applicant/accused could 
not submit whether some further treatment is 
advised to the daughter of the  applicant/accused. 
7. Having considered the submissions made 
by counsel for the respective parties, this Court 
does not find any good ground to extend the 
short term bail granted to the 
applicant/accused. Time Extension Application 
is, accordingly, dismissed. 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 08.12.2023

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Third Short Term Bail Application (IA) No.11 of 2026
In
Criminal Appeal No. 314 of 2021
Sandeep Singh ….......... Appellant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ……..... Respondent
Present : Mr. Nandan Arya, Advocate for the appellant.
 Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, Deputy Advocate General for the State. 
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and 
order dated 04.09.2021/06.09.2021, passed in Special Sessions 
Trial No.114 of 2017, State Vs. Sandeep Singh, by the court of 
FTC/Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge POCSO, Udham 
Singh Nagar. By it, the appellant has been convicted under 
Sections 376(2), 363, 366 IPC and sentenced accordingly. The 
appellant Sandeep Singh has filed a short term bail application on 
the ground that the daughter of the appellant has to undergo a 
surgery.
2. Heard on short term bail application.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the 
appellant’s daughter, who is a minor, has to undergo a surgery. 
Earlier also she had undergone a surgery, which has failed; now, 
repeat surgery for bone grafting is to be done; the doctor has 
prescribed to it; there is no one in the family to take care of the 
family of the appellant; his wife is back at home with minor 
children. Therefore, the appellant may be granted short term bail.
4. Learned State Counsel admits that the appellant’s wife 
is staying at home along with her minor children and one of the  2
children has to undergo a surgery. She would submit that the 
surgery is not scheduled.
5. When the Court required learned counsel for the 
appellant, as to why the date has not been fixed and as to why 
short term bail may be granted for the purpose of surgery? He 
submits that there is none in the family of the appellant even to 
take the date for surgery. 
6. Having considered, without adverting to the merits of 
the case, purely on the humanitarian ground, this Court is of the 
view that the appellant may be enlarged on short term bail for a 
period of six weeks from the date of his release. 
7. Let the appellant be released on short term bail for a 
period of six weeks from the date of his actual release, on his 
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties,

short term bail, the appellant shall surrender before the court 
concerned and intimation to that effect shall also be given to this
